name: Oxford Internet Institute

summary.text: The Oxford Internet Institute (OII) is a department of the University of Oxford. Its Digital Ethics Lab, directed by Luciano Floridi until 2023, produced the 2018 Nature Human Behaviour paper by Floridi and doctoral student Carl Öhman that proposed an ethical framework for the 'digital afterlife industry', and the OII publicised the 2019 projection that dead Facebook users could outnumber the living within decades.

sources.title: Professor Luciano Floridi and Carl Öhman publish ethical framework for the digital afterlife industry

facts.claim: The OII announced in 2018 that Professor Luciano Floridi and Carl Öhman had published an ethical framework for the digital afterlife industry, calling for dialogue between policymakers, industry and academics.

sources.title: Professor Luciano Floridi and Carl Öhman publish ethical framework for the digital afterlife industry
Professor Luciano Floridi and Carl Öhman publish ethical framework for the digital afterlife industry in Nature

facts.claim: Floridi served as Professor of Philosophy and Ethics of Information at the OII from May 2013 to July 2023 and directed its Digital Ethics Lab.
Öhman was a DPhil student at the OII from 2017 to 2020 and won its 2016 MSc thesis prize for work on the digital afterlife industry.

connections.claim: Floridi was an OII professor from 2013 to 2023.
Öhman was an OII doctoral candidate, 2017–2020.
